chunks: Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from ʿAli ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi. And the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Musa ibn ʿUmar, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:

Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام said: Ghusl is with one saʿ of water, and wudu (ablution) is with one mudd of water. The saʿ of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is five mudds, and the mudd is two hundred and eighty dirhams, and the dirham is six daniqs, and the daniq is the weight of six grains, and one grain is the weight of two barley grains of average size, neither from the small ones nor from the large ones.

key_terms.أَمْدَادٍ: plural of mudd, used to quantify the saʿ
key_terms.الغُسْلُ: ritual bath required in a state such as janabah
key_terms.الوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.حَبَّتَي شَعِيرٍ: two barley grains used as a fine unit of weight calibration
key_terms.دَوَانِيقَ: subdivisions of the dirham in weight measurement
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: a weight measure used to define the mudd
key_terms.صَاعٍ: a standard liquid measure used here for ghusl
key_terms.مُدٍّ: a smaller standard measure of water used here for wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: How much water is sufficient for ghusl and wudu (ablution) according to this hadith from al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith states the measured amount of water sufficient for ghusl and wudu (ablution), attributing the standard to the practice of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It also explains the weight-based measures used to define these quantities with precision for legal application in ritual purity.
